Project Objectives: The objective of this project is to evaluate, validate, and prepare for the field deployment of grid-forming (GFM) inverter technologies within a 380-MW hybrid facility integrating wind, solar, and battery energy storage. The work supports DOE’s national goals to maintain reliability under high IBR penetration by advancing the technical understanding of GFM-enabled stability services in large interconnected power systems. 6.1 Technical Goals and Expected Outcomes The primary goal of this project is to evaluate, validate, and prepare for the demonstration of mixed GFM and GFL inverter technologies at the 380-MW Wheatridge hybrid facility. Specific technical goals include: 1. Define and validate GFM performance metrics that quantify angle support, voltage regulation, frequency response, current-limiting behavior, and weak-grid stability. 2. Develop high-fidelity EMT models for GFM wind, GFM battery storage, GFL wind, and solar, including plant-level control interactions. 3. Conduct multi-stage EMT studies to evaluate mixed-resource behavior under weak-grid conditions, phase-angle disturbances, and system-level events. 4. Assess system reliability and operational risk through a structured Failure Modes and Effects Analysis (FMEA). 5. Develop a complete engineering, tuning, and commissioning plan for future activation of GFM capabilities at the site. 6. Establish validation frameworks and data-acquisition architecture to enable model-to-field comparison during a future demonstration. 7. Advance development of positive-sequence GFM models for planning and interconnection-level studies. Expected Outcomes BP1 work was designed to produce the following outcomes: • A validated and utility-ready set of GFM performance metrics. • High-fidelity EMT models and initial positive-sequence model components. • A comprehensive multi-stage EMT evaluation of mixed GFM/GFL interactions. • A 30-mode FMEA and risk-mitigation framework. Page 7 of 36 Award Number: DE-EE0010651 Recipient Name: Portland General Electric • Completed engineering design reviews, test plans, and commissioning procedures. • Installation and verification of site measurement and data infrastructure. • A reproducible methodology and modeling toolset supporting future GFM deployments. 6.2 Structure of Work and Relationship to the SOPO The project structure follows the DOE-approved Statement of Project Objectives (SOPO), which organizes activities into analytical studies, modeling and validation, engineering preparation, community benefits, and project management. • Tasks 1–3 establish performance metrics, complete EMT validation, and develop hybrid-plant models and HIL capabilities. • Tasks 4–7 address workforce development, engineering readiness, commissioning preparation, and site modifications. • Task 8 provides system-level EMT and model-validation support. Budget Period 2 (BP2), not initiated due to DOE termination, was intended to conduct a whole field demonstration, model calibration using high-resolution measurements, cost-benefit analysis of GFM upgrades, and final reporting. 7. Project Results and Discussion: This section summarizes the technical work and results completed in Budget Period 1 (BP1), organized according to the DOE-approved Statement of Project Objectives (SOPO). BP1 activities focused on developing GFM performance metrics, conducting multi-stage EMT studies, assembling and validating detailed models, preparing commissioning frameworks, and establishing measurement and site readiness. Together, these efforts provide the analytical and engineering foundation needed for future field demonstration. 7.1 Task 1 - GFM Pre-Demonstration Studies Task 1
